memoryText: Behold, I am with you and will keep you wherever you go.
readingInstruction: Today there is no new reading. The week you have completed followed Jacob, the deceiver, through his deepest crisis and into his transformation. Take time today to sit with the God who meets his people on the run.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Genesis 28:15 is the promise God spoke to Jacob at Bethel, to a man who had just deceived his father, stolen his brother’s blessing, and was fleeing for his life. He had nothing to commend him to God. And God said: “I am with you and will keep you wherever you go.”

This is grace at its purest. The promise is not conditional on Jacob’s behavior. It is unilateral. Notice the verbs, God will keep, God will bring, God will not leave. The promise rests entirely on God’s faithfulness, not on Jacob’s.

Say the verse to yourself. Hear the word “keep” as we heard it in Psalm 121 this week, the LORD as your keeper, never slumbering, watching over your going out and your coming in. Wherever you go, to work, into difficult relationships, into hard seasons, God is with you. By the end of this week, this verse should be your daily reminder that you are not alone.
weekInReview:
The week followed Jacob’s whole arc. You read his stealing of Esau’s blessing and his flight from home, and then the ladder vision at Bethel, where the covenant was renewed to a deceiver on the run. You watched him spend twenty years with Laban, marry Leah and Rachel, father eleven of the twelve tribes. You sang Psalm 121, the LORD as your keeper, and the Psalms of Ascent that followed. And then came Jacob’s wrestling at Peniel, where he received a new name: Israel. And finally his reunion with Esau, where the brother he had wronged ran to him with embrace and tears.

The week’s theme is transformation. Jacob the deceiver becomes Israel the striver. The man who manipulated for blessing learns to wrestle for it. And the God who began with him at Bethel keeps him through every twist of his road home.
reflectionQuestions: Where has God met you “on the run”, in a season when you did not deserve it? Jacob was fleeing his consequences when God appeared at Bethel. Not as a reward for his obedience, but as grace in the middle of his failure. Name a moment in your own life when God met you despite you. How does that memory shape how you receive his grace today?

How does Jacob’s wrestling at Peniel point you to Christ? Jacob wrestled with God and emerged with a new name, a permanent limp, and a blessing. The Christian’s wrestling with God in prayer is not a struggle against an enemy but a struggle with a Father, and through Christ, every wrestling believer emerges with a new name and a blessing too. Where are you wrestling right now? What blessing are you holding out for?

What does it mean that “God is with you wherever you go”? Today, take the promise of Genesis 28:15 into the specifics of your week, your work, your home, your hardest relationships, the places where you feel most alone. God is with you in each. What would change if you really believed this?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he meets people who have nothing to commend them, and tell him where you need him to meet you.
Ask him to wrestle with you where he must, not to destroy you but to bless you.
Rest this Sabbath in Christ, the true ladder between heaven and earth.
